systems.name: Euclid's postulates and common notions
systems.summary: The starting assumptions of the Elements, the model for axiomatic mathematics for two thousand years.

axioms.name: Postulate 1
axioms.text: A straight line can be drawn between any two points.

axioms.name: Postulate 2
axioms.text: A straight line segment can be extended indefinitely in a straight line.

axioms.name: Postulate 3
axioms.text: A circle can be drawn with any centre and any radius.

axioms.name: Postulate 4
axioms.text: All right angles are equal to one another.

axioms.name: Postulate 5 (parallel postulate)
axioms.text: If a line crossing two lines makes interior angles on one side summing to less than two right angles, the two lines meet on that side.

axioms.name: Common notion 1
axioms.text: Things equal to the same thing are equal to each other.

axioms.name: Common notion 2
axioms.text: If equals are added to equals, the wholes are equal.

axioms.name: Common notion 3
axioms.text: If equals are subtracted from equals, the remainders are equal.

axioms.name: Common notion 4
axioms.text: Things that coincide with one another are equal.

axioms.name: Common notion 5
axioms.text: The whole is greater than the part.

systems.name: Hilbert's axioms of geometry
systems.summary: A gap-free rebuild of Euclidean geometry from 'Foundations of Geometry', in five groups (later revised to 20 axioms).

axioms.name: I. Incidence (8 axioms)
axioms.text: Two points determine a line; three non-collinear points determine a plane; a line has at least two points; there exist at least four points not in one plane; and related rules about lines lying in planes.

axioms.name: II. Order (4 axioms)
axioms.text: 'Betweenness': if B is between A and C it is also between C and A; any two points have a point beyond; of three points on a line exactly one is between the others; Pasch's axiom: a line entering a triangle through one side leaves through another.

axioms.name: III. Congruence (5 axioms)
axioms.text: Segments and angles can be copied uniquely; congruence is transitive; adding congruent segments gives congruent segments; side-angle-side triangle congruence.

axioms.name: IV. Parallels (Playfair)
axioms.text: Through a point not on a line there is at most one line parallel to it.

axioms.name: V. Continuity (2 axioms)
axioms.text: Archimedes' axiom: any segment can be exceeded by repeating a smaller one; completeness: the line cannot be extended with new points while keeping the other axioms.

systems.name: Peano axioms
systems.summary: Define the natural numbers using only zero, a successor function S and induction.

axioms.name: Zero
axioms.text: 0 is a natural number.

axioms.name: Successor
axioms.text: Every natural number has a successor that is a natural number.

axioms.name: Zero is first
axioms.text: 0 is not the successor of any natural number.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>∀</mi><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.2222em" rspace="0.2222em">:</mo><mtext> </mtext><mi>S</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Injectivity
axioms.text: Different numbers have different successors.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>S</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>S</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Induction
axioms.text: If a property holds for 0, and holding for n implies it holds for S(n), it holds for every natural number.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mo fence="false" symmetric="true" minsize="1.2em" maxsize="1.2em">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>∧</mo><mi>∀</mi><mi>n</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mi>P</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo fence="false" symmetric="true" minsize="1.2em" maxsize="1.2em">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mi>∀</mi><mi>n</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>P</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>

systems.name: Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory with Choice (ZFC)
systems.summary: The standard foundation of modern mathematics: nearly every mathematical object can be built as a set from these axioms.

axioms.name: Extensionality
axioms.text: Two sets with the same members are equal.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>∀</mi><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>A</mi><mspace width="0.2778em"></mspace><mo stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mspace width="0.2778em"></mspace><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>B</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Empty set
axioms.text: There is a set with no members.

axioms.name: Pairing
axioms.text: For any a and b there is a set {a, b}.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>∃</mi><mi>C</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>∀</mi><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>C</mi><mspace width="0.2778em"></mspace><mo stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mspace width="0.2778em"></mspace><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∨</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Union
axioms.text: For any set of sets, there is a set of all their members.
axioms.tex: \exists U\,\forall x\,(x\in U\iff\exists Y\in\mathcal F:\ x\in Y)
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>∃</mi><mi>U</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>∀</mi><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>U</mi><mspace width="0.2778em"></mspace><mo stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mspace width="0.2778em"></mspace><mi>∃</mi><mi>Y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="mathcal">ℱ</mi><mo lspace="0.2222em" rspace="0.2222em">:</mo><mtext> </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Power set
axioms.text: For any set there is a set of all its subsets.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>∃</mi><mi>P</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>∀</mi><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>P</mi><mspace width="0.2778em"></mspace><mo stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mspace width="0.2778em"></mspace><mi>x</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi>A</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Infinity
axioms.text: There is a set containing ∅ and closed under x ↦ x ∪ {x}.
axioms.tex: \exists I\,\big(\varnothing\in I\land\forall x\in I:\ x\cup\{x\}\in I\big)
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>∃</mi><mi>I</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo fence="false" symmetric="true" minsize="1.2em" maxsize="1.2em">(</mo><mi>⌀</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>I</mi><mo>∧</mo><mi>∀</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0.2222em" rspace="0.2222em">:</mo><mtext> </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>∪</mo><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>x</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">}</mo><mo>∈</mo><mi>I</mi><mo fence="false" symmetric="true" minsize="1.2em" maxsize="1.2em">)</mo></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Separation (schema)
axioms.text: Any definable property cuts out a subset of a given set.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>∃</mi><mi>B</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>∀</mi><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>B</mi><mspace width="0.2778em"></mspace><mo stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mspace width="0.2778em"></mspace><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>∧</mo><mi>φ</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Replacement (schema)
axioms.text: The image of a set under a definable function is a set.

axioms.name: Regularity (foundation)
axioms.text: Every non-empty set has a member disjoint from it, so there are no infinite descending ∈-chains.

axioms.name: Choice
axioms.text: Every collection of non-empty sets has a choice function.
axioms.tex: \forall X\,\big(\varnothing\notin X\Rightarrow\exists f:X\to\textstyle\bigcup X,\ f(A)\in A\big)
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>∀</mi><mi>X</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mo fence="false" symmetric="true" minsize="1.2em" maxsize="1.2em">(</mo><mi>⌀</mi><mo>∉</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mi>∃</mi><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.2222em" rspace="0.2222em">:</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>→</mo><mstyle scriptlevel="0" displaystyle="false"><mo movablelimits="false">⋃</mo><mi>X</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mi>f</mi><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>∈</mo><mi>A</mi><mo fence="false" symmetric="true" minsize="1.2em" maxsize="1.2em">)</mo></mstyle></mrow></math>

systems.name: Field axioms
systems.summary: The rules shared by the rationals, the reals and the complex numbers.

axioms.name: Associativity
axioms.text: Addition and multiplication can be regrouped.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo separator="true">,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Commutativity
axioms.text: Order doesn't matter.

axioms.name: Identities
axioms.text: There are 0 and 1, and they differ.

axioms.name: Additive inverses
axioms.text: Every element has a negative.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false">−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Multiplicative inverses
axioms.text: Every non-zero element has a reciprocal.

axioms.name: Distributivity
axioms.text: Multiplication spreads over addition.

systems.name: Real numbers (complete ordered field)
systems.summary: The field axioms plus order and completeness pin down the real numbers uniquely.

axioms.name: Field axioms
axioms.text: The reals form a field.

axioms.name: Trichotomy
axioms.text: Exactly one of a < b, a = b, a > b holds.

axioms.name: Transitivity
axioms.text: a < b and b < c imply a < c.

axioms.name: Order and addition
axioms.text: a < b implies a + c < b + c.

axioms.name: Order and multiplication
axioms.text: a < b and c > 0 imply ac < bc.

axioms.name: Completeness
axioms.text: Every non-empty set bounded above has a least upper bound.

axioms.name: Closure
axioms.text: Combining two elements stays in the group.

axioms.name: Associativity
axioms.text: Grouping doesn't matter.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>c</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Identity
axioms.text: There is an element that changes nothing.

axioms.name: Inverses
axioms.text: Every element can be undone.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>∀</mi><mi>a</mi><mtext> </mtext><mi>∃</mi><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.2222em" rspace="0.2222em">:</mo><mtext> </mtext><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" stretchy="false" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></math>

axioms.name: (Abelian groups) Commutativity
axioms.text: Optional: order doesn't matter.

systems.name: Ring axioms
systems.summary: Integers, polynomials and matrices: addition forms an abelian group, multiplication is associative, and the two are linked by distributivity.

axioms.name: Additive abelian group
axioms.text: (R, +) is an abelian group with identity 0.

axioms.name: Associative multiplication
axioms.text: Multiplication can be regrouped.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Multiplicative identity
axioms.text: There is a 1 (in rings with unity).

axioms.name: Distributivity
axioms.text: Both sides.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></math>

systems.name: Vector space axioms
systems.summary: Vectors can be added and scaled by numbers from a field.

axioms.name: Additive abelian group
axioms.text: Vector addition is associative and commutative, with a zero vector and negatives.

axioms.name: Scalar compatibility
axioms.text: Scaling twice equals scaling by the product.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>𝐯</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝐯</mi></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Scalar identity
axioms.text: Scaling by 1 changes nothing.

systems.name: Inner product axioms
systems.summary: Add angles and lengths to a vector space.

axioms.name: Symmetry
axioms.text: Conjugate symmetric.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>u</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><menclose notation="top" class="tml-overline"><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>v</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>u</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></menclose></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Linearity
axioms.text: Linear in the first argument.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>w</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>u</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>w</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Positive definiteness
axioms.text: Only the zero vector has length zero.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>v</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext>for</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>v</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>

systems.name: Kolmogorov's probability axioms
systems.summary: Probability as a measure on a set of outcomes.

axioms.name: Non-negativity
axioms.text: Probabilities are never negative.

axioms.name: Unit measure
axioms.text: Something certainly happens.

axioms.name: Countable additivity
axioms.text: Disjoint events add.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="true">(</mo><msub><mo movablelimits="false">⋃</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Identity
axioms.text: Distance zero means the same point.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mspace width="0.2778em"></mspace><mo stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mspace width="0.2778em"></mspace><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Non-negativity
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Symmetry
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

axioms.name: Triangle inequality
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo separator="true">,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

systems.name: Topological space axioms
systems.summary: Nearness without distance: a chosen family of 'open' sets.

axioms.name: Extremes are open
axioms.text: The empty set and the whole space are open.

axioms.name: Unions
axioms.text: Any union of open sets is open.

axioms.name: Finite intersections
axioms.text: A finite intersection of open sets is open.

systems.name: Boolean algebra (Huntington postulates)
systems.summary: The algebra of true/false and of sets.

axioms.name: Commutativity
axioms.tex: a\lor b=b\lor a,\ a\land b=b\land a

axioms.name: Distributivity
axioms.text: Each operation distributes over the other.
axioms.mathml: <math><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∨</mo><mi>c</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∧</mo><mi>b</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∨</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" form="prefix" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>∧</mo><mi>c</mi><mo fence="true" form="postfix" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>

systems.name: Propositional logic (Łukasiewicz system)

proofs.name: √2 is irrational
steps: Suppose √2 = p/q with p, q whole numbers sharing no common factor.
Square both sides: 2 = p²/q², so p² = 2q².
So p² is even, which means p is even. Write p = 2k.
Then 4k² = 2q², so q² = 2k², which makes q even too.
Now p and q are both even, contradicting 'no common factor'.
So √2 cannot be written as a fraction. ∎

proofs.name: There are infinitely many primes
steps: Suppose there are only finitely many primes p₁, p₂, …, pₙ.
Form N = p₁·p₂·…·pₙ + 1.
Dividing N by any pᵢ leaves remainder 1, so no pᵢ divides N.
But N > 1 has at least one prime factor, which must be a prime not on the list.
This contradicts the list being complete. ∎

proofs.name: The real numbers are uncountable
steps: Suppose the reals between 0 and 1 could be listed r₁, r₂, r₃, … as decimals.
Build a new number x: make its nth digit different from the nth digit of rₙ (say 5 if that digit isn't 5, else 4).
x is between 0 and 1, yet it differs from every rₙ in the nth digit.
So x is missing from the list, and no list can contain all reals. ∎

proofs.name: Cantor's theorem
steps: Suppose f: A → 𝒫(A) is onto (hits every subset).
Let B = { a ∈ A : a ∉ f(a) }.
Since f is onto, B = f(b) for some b.
If b ∈ B then by definition b ∉ f(b) = B. If b ∉ B then b ∈ f(b) = B. Both are impossible.
So no such f exists: the power set is strictly larger. ∎

proofs.name: Sum of the first n numbers
steps: Write the sum forwards: S = 1 + 2 + … + n.
Write it backwards: S = n + (n−1) + … + 1.
Add the two lines column by column: each column sums to n + 1, and there are n columns.
So 2S = n(n + 1), giving S = n(n + 1)/2. ∎

proofs.name: Sum formula by induction
steps: Base case n = 1: the left side is 1 and the right side is 1·2/2 = 1.
Inductive step: assume the formula holds for n.
That is the formula for n + 1, so it holds for every n. ∎

proofs.name: Pythagorean theorem
steps: Place four copies of the right triangle inside a square of side a + b, hypotenuses facing inward.
The empty middle is a square of side c, area c².
Rearrange the same four triangles into two rectangles in the corner; now the empty space is two squares, a² and b².
The big square and the four triangles are unchanged, so the empty areas match: a² + b² = c². ∎

proofs.name: Angles of a triangle sum to 180°
steps: Draw the line through the top vertex parallel to the base.
The two angles it makes with the sides equal the two base angles (alternate angles).
Those two angles together with the top angle form a straight line, 180°.
So the three angles of the triangle sum to 180°. ∎ (Relies on the parallel postulate.)

proofs.name: The harmonic series diverges
steps: Group the terms: 1 + ½ + (⅓ + ¼) + (⅕ + … + ⅛) + …
Each group is at least ½: for example ⅓ + ¼ > ¼ + ¼ = ½.
There are infinitely many groups, each adding at least ½.
So the sum grows without bound. ∎

proofs.name: e is irrational
steps: Suppose e = p/q. Use e = Σ 1/k!.
Let x = q!·(e − Σ_{k=0}^{q} 1/k!). Since q!·e and q!/k! (k ≤ q) are integers, x is an integer.
So x is an integer strictly between 0 and 1, which is impossible. ∎
Subtract: 10x − x = 9, so 9x = 9 and x = 1.
Rigorously: 0.999… is the limit of 1 − 10⁻ⁿ, which is 1. ∎

proofs.name: The rationals are countable
steps: Arrange positive fractions p/q in a grid: row p, column q.
Walk the grid along diagonals p + q = 2, 3, 4, …, skipping fractions not in lowest terms.
Every positive fraction appears exactly once in this walk, so they can be numbered 1, 2, 3, …
Interleave 0 and the negatives to count all of ℚ. ∎

proofs.name: Fundamental theorem of arithmetic
steps: Existence: if n is prime, done. Otherwise n = ab with smaller a, b, which factor into primes by induction.
Euclid's lemma: if a prime p divides ab, it divides a or b (from Bézout's identity).
Uniqueness: if p₁…pₖ = q₁…qₘ, then p₁ divides some qⱼ, so p₁ = qⱼ.
Cancel it and repeat: the two factorizations match. ∎

proofs.name: Fermat's little theorem
steps: Consider a, 2a, …, (p−1)a modulo p.
None is 0 and no two are equal (if ia ≡ ja then p divides i − j), so they are 1, 2, …, p−1 in some order.
Multiply them: a^{p−1}·(p−1)! ≡ (p−1)! (mod p).
(p−1)! is not divisible by p, so cancel it: a^{p−1} ≡ 1. ∎

proofs.name: AM–GM for two numbers
steps: For a, b ≥ 0, (√a − √b)² ≥ 0 because squares are never negative.
Expand: a − 2√(ab) + b ≥ 0.
Rearrange: (a + b)/2 ≥ √(ab), with equality exactly when a = b. ∎

proofs.name: Pigeonhole: remainders repeat
proofs.tex: n+1\ \text{integers}\Rightarrow\text{two share a remainder mod } n
steps: Dividing by n gives only n possible remainders: 0, 1, …, n−1.
With n + 1 integers there are more numbers than remainders.
So two of them have the same remainder, and their difference is divisible by n. ∎

proofs.name: Odd-degree vertices come in pairs
steps: Count edge-ends: each edge has two ends, so Σ deg(v) = 2|E|, an even number.
Split the sum into even-degree and odd-degree vertices.
The even part is even, so the odd part must be even too.
A sum of odd numbers is even only when there is an even count of them. ∎

proofs.name: Finite geometric series
steps: Then rS = r + r² + … + r^{n}.
Subtract: S − rS = 1 − rⁿ, as everything else cancels.
Divide by 1 − r (r ≠ 1). ∎

proofs.name: Lagrange's theorem (groups)
steps: For a subgroup H, look at the cosets gH = { gh : h ∈ H }.
Each coset has exactly |H| elements (multiplying by g is one-to-one).
Two cosets are either identical or disjoint, so they split G into equal-sized pieces.
So |G| = (number of cosets) × |H|. ∎

proofs.name: The square of an odd number is odd
steps: Odd means n = 2k + 1 for some integer k.
That has the form 2m + 1, so n² is odd. ∎

proofs.name: log₂ 3 is irrational
steps: Suppose log₂ 3 = p/q with positive integers p, q.
Then 2^{p/q} = 3, so 2^p = 3^q.
The left side is even and the right side is odd.
That is impossible. ∎

proofs.name: Infinitely many primes of the form 4k + 3
steps: Suppose p₁, …, pₙ are all such primes. Let N = 4p₁⋯pₙ − 1, which is ≡ 3 (mod 4).
N is odd, so its prime factors are ≡ 1 or 3 (mod 4).
A product of numbers ≡ 1 (mod 4) is ≡ 1, so N has a prime factor ≡ 3.
That factor isn't any pᵢ (each pᵢ leaves remainder −1 dividing N), a contradiction. ∎

proofs.name: Euler's formula from power series
steps: Write e^{x} = Σ xⁿ/n! and put x = iθ.
Powers of i cycle: 1, i, −1, −i.
Collect the real terms: 1 − θ²/2! + θ⁴/4! − … = cos θ.
Collect the imaginary terms: θ − θ³/3! + … = sin θ. ∎

proofs.name: Derivative of x² from first principles
steps: f′(x) = lim_{h→0} ((x+h)² − x²)/h.
Expand: (x² + 2xh + h² − x²)/h = 2x + h.
As h → 0 this tends to 2x. ∎

proofs.name: A group has only one identity
steps: Suppose e and e′ are both identities.
e·e′ = e′ because e is an identity.
e·e′ = e because e′ is an identity.
So e = e′. ∎

proofs.name: A set of n elements has 2ⁿ subsets
steps: Line the elements up in order.
Each subset corresponds to an n-digit binary string: 1 if the element is in it, 0 if not.
This pairing is one-to-one and onto, and there are 2ⁿ such strings. ∎

proofs.name: Thales's theorem
steps: Let AB be a diameter with centre O and C on the circle.
OA = OB = OC (radii), so triangles OAC and OBC are isosceles.
Call their base angles α and β; triangle ABC then has angles α, β and α + β.
2α + 2β = 180°, so the angle at C is α + β = 90°. ∎

proofs.name: Interior angles of an n-gon
steps: From one vertex of a convex n-gon, draw diagonals to every non-adjacent vertex.
This cuts the polygon into n − 2 triangles.
Their angles fill the polygon's angles exactly, each triangle giving 180°. ∎

proofs.name: Russell's paradox
proofs.tex: R=\{x: x\notin x\}\ \text{is not a set}
steps: Naive set theory allows the set of all sets that do not contain themselves: R = { x : x ∉ x }.
If R ∈ R, then by definition R ∉ R.
If R ∉ R, then by definition R ∈ R.
Either way is a contradiction, so unrestricted comprehension must be dropped (ZFC uses Separation instead). ∎

proofs.name: The halting problem is undecidable
steps: Suppose a program H(P, x) always correctly answers whether program P halts on input x.
Build D(P): if H(P, P) says 'halts', loop forever; otherwise halt.
Run D on itself. If D(D) halts, H said it loops; if it loops, H said it halts.
Either way H is wrong, so no such H exists. ∎

proofs.name: √2 exists in the reals
steps: Let S = { x > 0 : x² < 2 }. S is non-empty (1 ∈ S) and bounded above by 2.
Completeness gives s = sup S.
If s² < 2, a slightly larger number is still in S, contradicting s being an upper bound.
If s² > 2, a slightly smaller number is still an upper bound, contradicting s being least. So s² = 2. ∎

theorems.sketch: Use Bézout's identity: if p ∤ a then px + ay = 1; multiply by b.

theorems.sketch: Strong induction for existence; Euclid's lemma for uniqueness.

theorems.sketch: Exhaustion with a geometric series 1 + 1/4 + 1/16 + ….

theorems.sketch: Exhaustion and a balancing (lever) argument.

theorems.statement: In a cyclic quadrilateral, the product of diagonals equals the sum of products of opposite sides.
theorems.sketch: Construct a point making two pairs of similar triangles.

theorems.name: Chinese remainder theorem
theorems.statement: Congruences with coprime moduli have a unique joint solution.
theorems.sketch: Build the answer from inverses of each modulus' complement.

theorems.name: Brahmagupta's identity
theorems.statement: (a² + nb²)(c² + nd²) is again of the form x² + ny².
theorems.sketch: Direct expansion, used to solve Pell equations.

theorems.name: Harmonic series divergence
theorems.statement: 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + … diverges.
theorems.sketch: Group terms into blocks each at least 1/2.

theorems.name: Cubic formula
theorems.statement: Cubic equations can be solved by radicals.
theorems.sketch: Substitute x = u + v and solve a quadratic in u³.

theorems.name: Quartic formula
theorems.statement: Quartic equations can be solved by radicals.
theorems.sketch: Reduce to a resolvent cubic.

theorems.name: Descartes' rule of signs
theorems.statement: Positive roots ≤ sign changes in the coefficients.
theorems.sketch: Induction using multiplication by (x − r).

theorems.name: Fermat's little theorem
theorems.statement: a^p ≡ a (mod p) for prime p.
theorems.sketch: The multiples of a permute the non-zero residues.

theorems.name: Pascal's theorem
theorems.statement: For a hexagon inscribed in a conic, the three meeting points of opposite sides lie on a line.
theorems.sketch: Projective transformations reduce it to a circle; Menelaus' theorem.

theorems.name: Fundamental theorem of calculus
theorems.statement: Integration and differentiation are inverse operations.
theorems.sketch: The derivative of the area function is the height of the curve.

theorems.name: Taylor's theorem
theorems.statement: Smooth functions are approximated by polynomials with a controllable remainder.
theorems.sketch: Repeated integration by parts or the mean value theorem.

theorems.name: Basel problem
theorems.statement: Σ 1/n² = π²/6.
theorems.sketch: Compare the product and series forms of sin x / x.

theorems.name: Seven Bridges of Königsberg
theorems.statement: A walk using every edge once exists only if 0 or 2 vertices have odd degree.
theorems.sketch: Each pass through a vertex uses two edge-ends.

theorems.name: Euler's polyhedron formula
theorems.statement: V − E + F = 2 for convex polyhedra.
theorems.sketch: Flatten to a planar graph and remove edges one at a time.

theorems.name: Wilson's theorem
theorems.statement: p is prime exactly when (p − 1)! ≡ −1 (mod p).
theorems.sketch: Pair each residue with its inverse; only 1 and −1 are self-inverse.

theorems.name: Lagrange's four-square theorem
theorems.statement: Every natural number is a sum of four squares.
theorems.sketch: Euler's four-square identity reduces it to primes; descent for primes.

theorems.name: Lagrange's theorem (groups)
theorems.statement: The order of a subgroup divides the order of the group.
theorems.sketch: Cosets partition the group into equal pieces.

theorems.name: Fundamental theorem of algebra
theorems.statement: Every non-constant complex polynomial has a root.
theorems.sketch: Many proofs; e.g. Liouville's theorem applied to 1/p(z).

theorems.name: Quadratic reciprocity
theorems.statement: Relates solvability of x² ≡ p (mod q) and x² ≡ q (mod p).
theorems.sketch: Gauss's lemma and counting lattice points.

theorems.name: Constructible polygons
theorems.statement: A regular n-gon is constructible with ruler and compass iff n is a power of 2 times distinct Fermat primes.
theorems.sketch: Constructible lengths lie in towers of quadratic extensions.

theorems.name: Abel–Ruffini theorem
theorems.statement: The general quintic has no solution by radicals.
theorems.sketch: The symmetric group S₅ is not solvable.

theorems.name: Galois's theorem
theorems.statement: A polynomial is solvable by radicals iff its Galois group is solvable.
theorems.sketch: Match field extensions with subgroups.

theorems.name: Cauchy's integral theorem
theorems.statement: The integral of an analytic function around a closed loop is 0.
theorems.sketch: Subdivide into small triangles (Goursat).

theorems.name: Cauchy's residue theorem
theorems.statement: Contour integrals equal 2πi times the sum of residues.
theorems.sketch: Shrink the contour to small circles around each pole.

theorems.name: Liouville's theorem (complex)
theorems.statement: A bounded entire function is constant.
theorems.sketch: Cauchy's estimate forces the derivative to vanish.

theorems.name: Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem
theorems.statement: Every bounded sequence of reals has a convergent subsequence.
theorems.sketch: Repeated halving of an interval containing infinitely many terms.

theorems.name: Intermediate value theorem
theorems.statement: A continuous function takes every value between f(a) and f(b).
theorems.sketch: Take the supremum of points where f is below the target.

theorems.name: Extreme value theorem
theorems.statement: A continuous function on [a, b] attains a maximum and minimum.
theorems.sketch: Compactness plus Bolzano–Weierstrass.

theorems.name: Mean value theorem
theorems.statement: Some point has slope equal to the average slope.
theorems.sketch: Apply Rolle's theorem to f minus the secant line.

theorems.name: Rolle's theorem
theorems.statement: If f(a) = f(b) then f′(c) = 0 somewhere in between.
theorems.sketch: Look at an interior maximum or minimum.

theorems.name: Heine–Borel theorem
theorems.statement: A subset of ℝⁿ is compact iff it is closed and bounded.
theorems.sketch: Bisection argument on an open cover.

theorems.name: Weierstrass approximation theorem
theorems.statement: Continuous functions on [a, b] are uniform limits of polynomials.
theorems.sketch: Bernstein polynomials or convolution with a smooth kernel.

theorems.name: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in progressions
theorems.statement: If gcd(a, d) = 1 there are infinitely many primes ≡ a (mod d).
theorems.sketch: L-functions do not vanish at s = 1.

theorems.name: Prime number theorem
theorems.statement: π(x) ~ x / ln x.
theorems.sketch: Show ζ(s) has no zeros on Re(s) = 1.

theorems.name: Bertrand's postulate
theorems.statement: There is always a prime between n and 2n.
theorems.sketch: Bounds on the central binomial coefficient.

theorems.name: Cantor's diagonal theorem
theorems.statement: The real numbers are uncountable.
theorems.sketch: Build a number differing from the nth listed number in the nth digit.

theorems.name: Cantor's theorem
theorems.statement: Every set is smaller than its power set.
theorems.sketch: The set of elements not in their own image is missed.

theorems.name: Schröder–Bernstein theorem
theorems.statement: Injections both ways give a bijection.
theorems.sketch: Trace chains of back-and-forth images.

theorems.name: Transcendence of e
theorems.statement: e is not a root of any integer polynomial.
theorems.sketch: Construct integrals that would give an integer strictly between 0 and 1.

theorems.name: Transcendence of π

theorems.sketch: Lindemann–Weierstrass theorem applied to e^{iπ} = −1.

theorems.name: Lindemann–Weierstrass theorem
theorems.statement: e^α is transcendental for algebraic α ≠ 0.
theorems.sketch: Hermite-style auxiliary functions.

theorems.sketch: Triangulate and sum angle excesses.

theorems.statement: Gaussian curvature is intrinsic: it doesn't change under bending.
theorems.sketch: Express curvature using only the metric.

theorems.name: Riemann mapping theorem
theorems.statement: Every simply connected proper open subset of ℂ maps conformally onto the disk.
theorems.sketch: Extremal problem over normal families.

theorems.name: Sylow theorems
theorems.statement: Subgroups of prime-power order exist and are conjugate, with counts ≡ 1 (mod p).
theorems.sketch: Group actions on subsets and cosets.

theorems.name: Cayley's theorem

theorems.sketch: Let the group act on itself by multiplication.

theorems.name: Hilbert's basis theorem

theorems.sketch: Induct on the number of variables using leading coefficients.

theorems.statement: Ideals and algebraic sets correspond over algebraically closed fields.
theorems.sketch: Noether normalization or the Rabinowitsch trick.

theorems.statement: A simple closed curve splits the plane into inside and outside.
theorems.sketch: Approximate by polygons; homology in general.

theorems.statement: A continuous tangent vector field on a sphere must vanish somewhere.
theorems.sketch: Euler characteristic of the sphere is 2, not 0.

theorems.statement: A contraction on a complete metric space has exactly one fixed point.
theorems.sketch: Iterate; the sequence is Cauchy.

theorems.name: Hahn–Banach theorem
theorems.statement: Bounded linear functionals extend from subspaces.
theorems.sketch: Extend one dimension at a time, then Zorn's lemma.

theorems.name: Spectral theorem
theorems.statement: Symmetric (self-adjoint) matrices are diagonalizable with orthonormal eigenvectors.
theorems.sketch: Find one eigenvector, restrict to its orthogonal complement, repeat.

theorems.name: Cayley–Hamilton theorem
theorems.statement: A matrix satisfies its characteristic polynomial.
theorems.sketch: Adjugate identity (λI − A)·adj = det·I.

theorems.name: Rank–nullity theorem
theorems.statement: dim(image) + dim(kernel) = dim(domain).
theorems.sketch: Extend a kernel basis to a full basis.

theorems.name: Jordan normal form
theorems.statement: Over ℂ every matrix is similar to a block-diagonal Jordan form.
theorems.sketch: Generalized eigenspaces and nilpotent structure.

theorems.name: Perron–Frobenius theorem
theorems.statement: A positive matrix has a unique largest positive eigenvalue with a positive eigenvector.
theorems.sketch: Collatz–Wielandt formula or fixed points on the simplex.

theorems.name: Law of large numbers
theorems.statement: Sample averages converge to the expected value.
theorems.sketch: Chebyshev's inequality for the weak law.

theorems.name: Central limit theorem
theorems.statement: Normalized sums of independent variables tend to a normal distribution.
theorems.sketch: Characteristic functions converge to e^{−t²/2}.

theorems.name: Bayes' theorem
theorems.statement: P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B).
theorems.sketch: Write P(A∩B) two ways.

theorems.name: Kolmogorov's zero–one law
theorems.statement: Tail events of independent sequences have probability 0 or 1.
theorems.sketch: A tail event is independent of itself.

theorems.name: Ergodic theorem
theorems.statement: Time averages equal space averages for ergodic systems.
theorems.sketch: Maximal ergodic lemma.

theorems.name: Noether's theorem
theorems.statement: Every continuous symmetry of an action gives a conservation law.
theorems.sketch: Vary the action along the symmetry.

theorems.name: Gödel's completeness theorem
theorems.statement: Every logically valid first-order statement is provable.
theorems.sketch: Build a model from a maximal consistent set (Henkin).

theorems.name: Gödel's first incompleteness theorem
theorems.statement: Any consistent, effective system containing arithmetic has true but unprovable statements.
theorems.sketch: Encode 'this sentence is not provable' arithmetically.

theorems.name: Gödel's second incompleteness theorem
theorems.statement: Such a system cannot prove its own consistency.
theorems.sketch: Formalize the first theorem inside the system.

theorems.name: Undecidability of the halting problem
theorems.statement: No algorithm decides whether every program halts.
theorems.sketch: Diagonalization: run the decider on a self-referential program.

theorems.name: Church–Turing thesis
theorems.statement: Effective computability equals Turing computability.
theorems.sketch: A thesis, not a theorem: supported by every model agreeing.

theorems.name: Löwenheim–Skolem theorem
theorems.statement: A countable first-order theory with an infinite model has models of every infinite size.
theorems.sketch: Skolem functions and compactness.

theorems.name: Compactness theorem
theorems.statement: A set of sentences has a model if every finite subset does.
theorems.sketch: Follows from completeness.

theorems.name: Independence of the continuum hypothesis
theorems.statement: CH can be neither proved nor disproved in ZFC.
theorems.sketch: Gödel's constructible universe; Cohen's forcing.

theorems.name: Zorn's lemma ⇔ axiom of choice
theorems.statement: If every chain has an upper bound, a maximal element exists.
theorems.sketch: Transfinite recursion using a choice function.

theorems.name: Well-ordering theorem
theorems.statement: Every set can be well-ordered (equivalent to choice).
theorems.sketch: Choose least elements step by step through the ordinals.

theorems.name: Banach–Tarski paradox
theorems.statement: A ball can be cut into finitely many pieces and reassembled into two identical balls.
theorems.sketch: Paradoxical decomposition of the free group of rotations; needs choice.

theorems.name: Arrow's impossibility theorem
theorems.statement: No ranked voting rule with 3+ options satisfies all of Arrow's fairness conditions.
theorems.sketch: Find a pivotal voter who becomes a dictator.

theorems.name: Nash's existence theorem
theorems.statement: Every finite game has a mixed-strategy equilibrium.
theorems.sketch: Kakutani's fixed-point theorem.

theorems.name: Von Neumann's minimax theorem
theorems.statement: Zero-sum two-player games have a value.
theorems.sketch: Convexity and a separating hyperplane.

theorems.name: Shannon's source coding theorem
theorems.statement: Data cannot be compressed below its entropy on average.
theorems.sketch: Typical sequences.

theorems.name: Noisy-channel coding theorem
theorems.statement: Reliable communication is possible at any rate below channel capacity.
theorems.sketch: Random codes and typicality.

theorems.name: Four colour theorem
theorems.statement: Every planar map can be coloured with four colours.
theorems.sketch: Computer check of 1,936 unavoidable configurations.

theorems.name: Five colour theorem
theorems.statement: Every planar map can be coloured with five colours.
theorems.sketch: A planar graph has a vertex of degree ≤ 5; Kempe chains.

theorems.name: Kuratowski's theorem
theorems.statement: A graph is planar iff it contains no subdivision of K₅ or K₃,₃.
theorems.sketch: Minimal non-planar graphs analysed directly.

theorems.name: Hall's marriage theorem
theorems.statement: A perfect matching exists iff every group of k people likes at least k partners.
theorems.sketch: Induction on the number of people.

theorems.name: Ramsey's theorem
theorems.statement: Large enough structures contain ordered substructures, e.g. R(3,3) = 6.
theorems.sketch: Induction with the pigeonhole principle.

theorems.name: Dilworth's theorem
theorems.statement: In a finite poset, the largest antichain equals the fewest chains covering it.
theorems.sketch: Induction, or König's theorem on bipartite graphs.

theorems.name: Erdős–Szekeres theorem
theorems.statement: Any sequence of n² + 1 distinct numbers has a monotone subsequence of length n + 1.
theorems.sketch: Pigeonhole on (longest increasing, longest decreasing) labels.

theorems.name: Sperner's lemma
theorems.statement: A properly labelled triangulation has a fully labelled cell.
theorems.sketch: Parity count of doors in a walk.

theorems.name: Fermat's Last Theorem
theorems.statement: xⁿ + yⁿ = zⁿ has no positive integer solutions for n > 2.
theorems.sketch: Modularity of semistable elliptic curves rules out Frey's curve.

theorems.name: Modularity theorem
theorems.statement: Every rational elliptic curve is modular.
theorems.sketch: Galois representations and modularity lifting.

theorems.name: Catalan's conjecture (Mihăilescu)
theorems.statement: 8 and 9 are the only consecutive perfect powers.
theorems.sketch: Cyclotomic fields and Galois modules.

theorems.name: Green–Tao theorem
theorems.statement: The primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
theorems.sketch: Relative Szemerédi theorem with a pseudorandom majorant.

theorems.name: Szemerédi's theorem
theorems.statement: Sets of positive density contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
theorems.sketch: Regularity lemma; ergodic proof by Furstenberg.

theorems.name: Bounded prime gaps
theorems.statement: Infinitely many prime pairs differ by at most 246.
theorems.sketch: Sieve methods (GPY, Maynard weights).

theorems.name: Weak Goldbach conjecture
theorems.statement: Every odd number greater than 5 is a sum of three primes.
theorems.sketch: Circle method plus computer verification for small cases.

theorems.name: Poincaré conjecture
theorems.statement: Every simply connected closed 3-manifold is the 3-sphere.
theorems.sketch: Ricci flow with surgery.

theorems.name: Geometrization theorem
theorems.statement: Every closed 3-manifold splits into pieces with one of eight geometries.
theorems.sketch: Ricci flow with surgery.

theorems.name: Classification of surfaces
theorems.statement: Closed surfaces are spheres with handles or crosscaps.
theorems.sketch: Triangulate and cut into a normal-form polygon.

theorems.name: Classification of finite simple groups
theorems.statement: Every finite simple group is cyclic, alternating, of Lie type, or one of 26 sporadic groups.
theorems.sketch: Tens of thousands of pages over decades.

theorems.name: Feit–Thompson theorem
theorems.statement: Every finite group of odd order is solvable.
theorems.sketch: Character theory and local analysis (255 pages).

theorems.name: Kepler conjecture
theorems.statement: No packing of equal spheres is denser than the face-centred cubic packing.
theorems.sketch: Computer-assisted linear programming; formally verified 2014.

theorems.name: Isoperimetric inequality
theorems.statement: Of all closed curves of a given length, the circle encloses the most area.
theorems.sketch: Steiner symmetrization or Fourier series (Hurwitz).

theorems.name: Pick's theorem
theorems.statement: Lattice polygon area = interior points + boundary/2 − 1.
theorems.sketch: Additivity: check triangles and glue.

theorems.name: Morley's trisector theorem
theorems.statement: Adjacent angle trisectors of any triangle meet in an equilateral triangle.
theorems.sketch: Build the equilateral triangle first and work backwards.

theorems.name: Desargues's theorem
theorems.statement: Two triangles in perspective from a point are in perspective from a line.
theorems.sketch: Lift to 3D, where it is immediate.

theorems.name: Sylvester–Gallai theorem
theorems.statement: Points not all on a line determine a line through exactly two of them.
theorems.sketch: Take the point–line pair at minimum distance.

theorems.name: Napoleon's theorem
theorems.statement: Centres of equilateral triangles built on a triangle's sides form an equilateral triangle.
theorems.sketch: Complex numbers with cube roots of unity.

theorems.name: Stokes' theorem
theorems.statement: The integral of dω over a region equals the integral of ω over its boundary.
theorems.sketch: Prove for small cubes and let interior faces cancel.

theorems.name: Divergence theorem
theorems.statement: Total divergence inside equals flux out through the boundary.
theorems.sketch: Special case of Stokes.

theorems.name: Implicit function theorem
theorems.statement: F(x, y) = 0 defines y as a smooth function of x near a point where ∂F/∂y is invertible.
theorems.sketch: Contraction mapping.

theorems.name: Inverse function theorem
theorems.statement: A smooth map with invertible derivative is locally invertible.
theorems.sketch: Contraction mapping on a neighbourhood.

theorems.name: Picard–Lindelöf theorem
theorems.statement: Lipschitz ODEs have unique local solutions.
theorems.sketch: Iterate the integral equation (contraction).

theorems.name: Stone–Weierstrass theorem
theorems.statement: Separating subalgebras are dense in continuous functions on a compact space.
theorems.sketch: Approximate |x| by polynomials, then use lattice operations.

theorems.name: Arzelà–Ascoli theorem
theorems.statement: Equicontinuous bounded families have uniformly convergent subsequences.
theorems.sketch: Diagonal argument on a countable dense set.

theorems.name: Riesz representation theorem
theorems.statement: Continuous linear functionals on a Hilbert space are inner products with a fixed vector.
theorems.sketch: Project onto the kernel's orthogonal complement.

theorems.name: Open mapping theorem
theorems.statement: A surjective bounded operator between Banach spaces is open.
theorems.sketch: Baire category theorem.

theorems.name: Baire category theorem
theorems.statement: A complete metric space is not a countable union of nowhere-dense sets.
theorems.sketch: Nested balls avoiding each set.

theorems.name: Lebesgue dominated convergence
theorems.statement: Limits and integrals commute under an integrable bound.
theorems.sketch: Fatou's lemma applied twice.

theorems.name: Radon–Nikodym theorem
theorems.statement: An absolutely continuous measure has a density.
theorems.sketch: Hilbert-space argument (von Neumann) or Hahn decomposition.

theorems.name: Fourier inversion theorem
theorems.statement: A function is recovered from its Fourier transform.
theorems.sketch: Gaussian approximate identities.

theorems.name: Plancherel theorem
theorems.statement: The Fourier transform preserves the L² norm.
theorems.sketch: Dense subspace then extend.

theorems.name: Nyquist–Shannon sampling theorem
theorems.statement: A signal band-limited to B is determined by samples at rate 2B.
theorems.sketch: Periodize the spectrum; sinc interpolation.

theorems.name: Atiyah–Singer index theorem
theorems.statement: The analytic index of an elliptic operator equals a topological index.
theorems.sketch: K-theory and cobordism.

theorems.name: Riemann–Roch theorem
theorems.statement: ℓ(D) − ℓ(K − D) = deg D − g + 1 on a curve of genus g.
theorems.sketch: Serre duality and sheaf cohomology.

theorems.name: Bézout's theorem
theorems.statement: Two plane curves of degrees m and n meet in mn points (counted properly).
theorems.sketch: Resultants.

theorems.name: Mordell's theorem
theorems.statement: Rational points on an elliptic curve form a finitely generated group.
theorems.sketch: Weak Mordell–Weil plus height descent.

theorems.name: Faltings's theorem
theorems.statement: Curves of genus ≥ 2 have finitely many rational points.
theorems.sketch: Shafarevich and Tate conjectures for abelian varieties.

theorems.name: Hasse–Minkowski theorem
theorems.statement: A quadratic form has a rational solution iff it does over ℝ and every p-adic field.
theorems.sketch: Reduction on the number of variables.

theorems.name: Minkowski's convex body theorem
theorems.statement: A symmetric convex body of volume > 2ⁿ contains a non-zero lattice point.
theorems.sketch: Translate copies overlap by pigeonhole (Blichfeldt).

theorems.name: Dirichlet's approximation theorem
theorems.statement: Every real has infinitely many fractions p/q within 1/q².
theorems.sketch: Pigeonhole on fractional parts.

theorems.name: Roth's theorem
theorems.statement: Algebraic irrationals can't be approximated much better than 1/q².
theorems.sketch: Auxiliary polynomials with many vanishing derivatives.

theorems.name: Lagrange's continued fraction theorem
theorems.statement: A real number has a periodic continued fraction iff it is a quadratic irrational.
theorems.sketch: Bounded reduced forms.

theorems.name: Monotone convergence theorem
theorems.statement: A bounded monotone sequence of reals converges.
theorems.sketch: Converges to its supremum (completeness).

theorems.name: Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
theorems.sketch: The quadratic ‖u + tv‖² ≥ 0 has non-positive discriminant.

theorems.name: Jensen's inequality
theorems.statement: f(E[X]) ≤ E[f(X)] for convex f.
theorems.sketch: Supporting line at the mean.

theorems.name: Hölder's inequality
theorems.statement: ∫|fg| ≤ ‖f‖_p ‖g‖_q with 1/p + 1/q = 1.
theorems.sketch: Young's inequality ab ≤ aᵖ/p + b^q/q.

theorems.name: Isoperimetric problem of Dido
theorems.statement: Among curves of fixed length the circle maximizes area.
theorems.sketch: Euler–Lagrange equation with a constraint.

theorems.name: Euler–Lagrange theorem
theorems.statement: Stationary paths of an action satisfy the Euler–Lagrange equation.
theorems.sketch: Vary the path and integrate by parts.

theorems.name: Brachistochrone
theorems.statement: The fastest descent curve under gravity is a cycloid.
theorems.sketch: Fermat's principle of least time in a varying medium.

theorems.name: Squaring the circle is impossible
theorems.statement: No ruler-and-compass construction of a square with the area of a given circle.
theorems.sketch: π is transcendental, but constructible numbers are algebraic.

theorems.name: Doubling the cube is impossible
theorems.statement: ∛2 cannot be constructed with ruler and compass.
theorems.sketch: Its minimal polynomial has degree 3, not a power of 2.

theorems.name: Angle trisection is impossible
theorems.statement: A 60° angle cannot be trisected with ruler and compass.
theorems.sketch: cos 20° satisfies an irreducible cubic.

theorems.name: Euler's theorem (number theory)
theorems.statement: a^φ(n) ≡ 1 (mod n) when gcd(a, n) = 1.
theorems.sketch: Multiplying by a permutes the units mod n.

theorems.name: Lucas's theorem
theorems.statement: Binomial coefficients mod p follow the base-p digits.
theorems.sketch: Expand (1 + x)ⁿ mod p using the Frobenius map.

theorems.name: Burnside's lemma
theorems.statement: Number of orbits = average number of fixed points.
theorems.sketch: Double count pairs (g, x) with gx = x.

theorems.name: Pólya enumeration theorem
theorems.statement: Counts colourings up to symmetry with a cycle-index polynomial.
theorems.sketch: Weighted Burnside's lemma.

theorems.name: Cook–Levin theorem
theorems.statement: Boolean satisfiability is NP-complete.
theorems.sketch: Encode any polynomial-time verifier's run as a formula.

theorems.name: Rice's theorem
theorems.statement: Every non-trivial property of what programs compute is undecidable.
theorems.sketch: Reduce the halting problem to it.

theorems.name: Time hierarchy theorem
theorems.statement: More time lets machines decide strictly more problems.
theorems.sketch: Diagonalize against faster machines with a clock.

theorems.name: PCP theorem
theorems.who: Arora; Safra; Lund; Motwani; Sudan; Szegedy
theorems.statement: Every NP proof can be checked by reading a constant number of random bits.
theorems.sketch: Algebraic coding; later Dinur's gap amplification.
